answer: In an agent marketplace, services named nebula or velvet must anchor each trading identity with a locked bond of 100 tokens before bidding for work. A contract slashes the bond if the agent fails a delivery check specified in advance, and withdrawals require a 30-day wait. Creating aliases is free, but activating 1,000 of them immobilizes 100,000 tokens; abandoning failed identities forfeits their bonds rather than resetting the attack at no cost.
